- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates, especially in later 30d; increase forecast for 15-30d horizon.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00), producing exaggerated overshoots in 30d forecast — cap or dampen such spikes.
- Mean reversion is evident: if 30d forecast is >1.5x historical mean, reduce by 20-40% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Sentiment history with alternating 0.67/0.33 patterns suggests model should not follow sentiment extremes — average or smooth transitions between high/low sentiment periods.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows sharp late-period spikes (e.g., >10% increase from day 20-30), model often underestimates — adjust upward by 10-30% if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3-5 days, model tends to overforecast — reduce forecast by 15-25% for 30d horizon.
- Avoid forecasting extreme values (e.g., >10x historical max) unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) and recent price is rising.
